# xshield_enforcement_status (Data Source)

Reports whether an account and region have converged on the policy Xshield expects, what the next enforcement run would change, and what the cloud connector observes that differs from what was applied.

It reads only, so it can run inside a `check` block. Where checks are evaluated on a schedule, such as HCP Terraform continuous validation, that alerts on drift and stalled pipelines without anyone running an apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Alert on drift, stalled pipelines and workloads Xshield could not enforce.
# Checks run on every plan and, where the platform evaluates them on a
# schedule, between runs too.
check "xshield_enforcement" {
  data "xshield_enforcement_status" "this" {
    cloud_account_id = "123456789012"
    region           = "us-east-1"
  }

  assert {
    condition = length([for f in data.xshield_enforcement_status.this.drift_findings : f if f.severity == "high"]) == 0
    error_message = join("\n", [
      for f in data.xshield_enforcement_status.this.drift_findings : "${f.kind} ${f.resource}: ${f.detail} (fixed by: ${f.restoration})" if f.severity == "high"
    ])
  }

  assert {
    condition     = data.xshield_enforcement_status.this.state != "pending" || timecmp(timeadd(data.xshield_enforcement_status.this.pending_since, "24h"), plantimestamp()) > 0
    error_message = "Approved policy has waited more than 24 hours for an enforcement run."
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cloud_account_id` (String) Cloud account to report on.
- `region` (String) Region to report on.

### Read-Only

- `applied_at` (String) When the latest receipt was recorded.
- `applied_content_hash` (String) Content hash in the latest apply receipt.
- `applied_version` (Number) Version in the latest apply receipt. Null when nothing has been applied.
- `drift_evaluated` (Boolean) Whether drift could be evaluated: it needs an applied receipt and a cloud connector observation taken after it. An observation older than the latest apply describes resources that apply replaced, so it is not evaluated.
- `drift_findings` (List of Object) Differences between the cloud as observed and the snapshot as applied. `kind`: what differs, such as `ruleMissing`, `ruleUnmanaged` or `memberUnattached`. `severity`: `high` where access may be wider than approved or a workload is unenforced, otherwise `medium`. `restoration`: `pipeline` when the next enforcement apply restores it, `manual` when Terraform cannot see it and it must be removed by hand, `workload` when the owning workspace's attachment must change. `resource`: AWS ID of the affected resource, or the Xshield asset ID for an attachment finding. `key`: snapshot key involved, when there is one. `detail`: human-readable explanation. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--drift_findings))
- `drift_observed_at` (String) When the cloud connector's latest observation was taken.
- `expected_content_hash` (String) Content hash of the expected snapshot.
- `expected_version` (Number) Version Xshield expects to be enforced.
- `last_checked_at` (String) When an enforcement plan last resolved the expected version. A stale value means the pipeline has stopped running, whatever the convergence state says.
- `notices` (List of Object) What Xshield could not enforce in the latest version, and why. A workload with a refusal carries no Xshield group until the cause is fixed. `code`: `assetRefused`, `assetContained`, `groupRefused` or `withdrawing`. `reason`: the cloud connector's refusal code, as the Xshield portal shows it, such as `NO_FREE_SLOT` or `RULE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED:inbound/ipv4=61`. `asset_id`, `group`: the Xshield asset, or the security group key, the notice is about, when there is one. `message`: what happened and what it means for the workload. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--notices))
- `pending_attachments_added` (List of String) Keys of interface attachments the next enforcement run will create.
- `pending_rules_added` (List of String) Keys of rules the next enforcement run will add.
- `pending_rules_removed` (List of String) Keys of rules the next enforcement run will remove.
- `pending_security_groups_added` (List of String) Keys of security groups the next enforcement run will create.
- `pending_since` (String) When the oldest policy change not yet applied was published.
- `published` (Boolean) False while Xshield has published nothing for this account and region. `state` is then `unpublished`, versions are null and every list is empty, so checks stay quiet.
- `state` (String) `converged` when the latest receipt matches the expected snapshot, `pending` when Xshield expects newer policy than was applied, `unapplied` when nothing has been applied yet, `unpublished` when Xshield has published nothing to apply.
